checks: The small-excess branch gives δ≤2Δ/V<ε/(8d²) and dδ<ε/16. The coordinate-face exterior pyramid has volume V(1−ε^(d−1))(−x_i). The top-face exterior pyramid has volume V(sum_i x_i−1), with the two √d factors canceling.

The d vertices with a coordinate at least one are distinct by the upper sum and coordinate lower bounds. Their sums exceed ε. The minimizing vertex v_0 has sum at most ε and is the only remaining vertex.

The barycentric coefficient α_0 for εe_i is positive, with (1−α_0)/α_0≤(ε+dδ)/(1−ε−dδ). For each coordinate j, the choice i≠j bounds its v_0 coordinate by δ times this ratio. The summed constant is less than (17/239)ε², hence less than ε²/4.

The reflected simplex defining P has lower facet area √d(da−ε)^(d−1)/(d−1)!. Its exterior pyramid from v_0 gives the asserted volume after scaling. At d=2, da−ε>1, and at d≥3, da−ε>2. Thus the lower bound εV/8 suffices in the small-excess branch.

The original source a585520b0a2a14db §2 gives the same hypotheses, both branches, and the same all-dimensional constant. The archived rational script passed 72 source and constant cases, 120 perturbed enclosures, and 102 small-excess cases.

overlap.comparison: At d=2 the sets A,P, arbitrary triangle R and arbitrary compact convex L are identical. The left side is identical because 2^(−d)=1/4. The accepted ε/16 bound implies the frozen ε/128 bound in this specialization. It gives no enclosing d-simplex estimate in d≥3.

readability: The upper facet cone is invoked only for a positive violation of its supporting inequality. The reflected lower facet of P then uses the opposite side. The stated signs and scale factors are correct.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The geometric proof applies to every enclosing simplex in dimension d≥2 and gives the stated constant. The planar instance is already covered by a stronger accepted estimate.
